advances: Removes every conditional mean, energy, and pair-count restriction from the original-law actual-depth product theorem of 9b5e06469756fd2e. Unbounded-count overlapping unions share its label-selection budget, while all remaining two-overlap unions share one fixed full-row price bound. These two blocks are combined before the reflected product source and the exact occupied-capacity leaf transfer. This proves the unrestricted two-midpoint-center product moment theorem, not the locked mixed-integer-volume conjecture.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None. Only the seven declared accepted predecessors are used, with the explicit alias and normalization maps above. All product selection, combination of the two blocks, actual-depth source, and original-law occupied-capacity transfer are proved here.
proof:
We retain the notation of 9b5e06469756fd2e for the original laws, cores, conditional unions, and occupied capacities. Its scalar constant \(B\) is the \(B\) in (4), and its label constant \(C\) is our \(C_{\mathrm{label}}\). We will use its scalar inequality (8) only on its already proved domain, and prove the additional coverage from abb26eb9816cdb80 and 4b01e775176a9049. The bounded-count full-row estimate will instead come from c00bd51b9e53801c.

First construct the exact parity-disjoint partition. Convexity gives \(\operatorname{conv}(A_i)\subseteq Q_i\), hence \(A_i=\operatorname{conv}(A_i)\cap\mathbb Z^{n_i}\). If \(\mathcal C_i\) is empty, all atoms have different parity classes, since a distinct same-parity pair would give an integral midpoint center. Partition \(A_i\) into singletons of capacity one.

If \(\mathcal C_i=\lbrace c_i\rbrace\), set \(R_i=A_i\cap(2c_i-A_i)\). The one-center geometry proved in 60336390757d4ce6 gives a complete convex lattice core symmetric about \(c_i\), with occupied count \(M_i=(|R_i|+1)/2\). Every outside atom is the sole member of its parity class in the entire support. Partition into \(R_i\), of capacity \(M_i\), and the individual outside atoms, of capacity one. Thus the total capacity is exactly \(K_i\).

If \(\mathcal C_i=\lbrace c_{i,0},c_{i,1}\rbrace\), put
$$
\begin{aligned}
R_{i,a}&=A_i\cap(2c_{i,a}-A_i),&
M_{i,a}&=(|R_{i,a}|+1)/2,&
m_{i,a}&=M_{i,a}-1,\\
U_i&=R_{i,0}\cup R_{i,1},&
q_{\mathrm{ov},i}&=|R_{i,0}\cap R_{i,1}|,&
s_i&=|A_i\setminus U_i|.
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
$$
Accepted fact 9e1805a461c7be2c applies to the complete support just established. Its overlap \(t\) is our \(q_{\mathrm{ov},i}\); its \(A,c_a,R_a,M_a,s\) are \(A_i,c_{i,a},R_{i,a},M_{i,a},s_i\). It proves that \(m_{i,a}\ge1\), every parity class has at most two atoms, the centers have different parity, and both the atom intersection and the occupied-parity intersection of the cores have size \(q_{\mathrm{ov},i}\in\lbrace0,1,2\rbrace\). Every outside atom has its own parity class, disjoint from those of \(U_i\). In particular the exact occupied count of the union is
\(k_{i,U_i}=M_{i,0}+M_{i,1}-q_{\mathrm{ov},i}\), and \(K_i=k_{i,U_i}+s_i\).

For \(q_{\mathrm{ov},i}=0\), partition into the two disjoint cores, of capacities \(M_{i,0},M_{i,1}\), and outside singletons. For \(q_{\mathrm{ov},i}\in\lbrace1,2\rbrace\), partition into \(U_i\), of capacity \(k_{i,U_i}\), and outside singletons. Denote each resulting partition by \(\mathcal D_i\), with piece capacities \(k_{i,D}\). In all cases the partition is disjoint both in atoms and in occupied parity classes, so
\(\sum_{D\in\mathcal D_i}k_{i,D}=K_i\le2^{n_i}\).

An overlapping union \(U_i\) is closed under integral midpoints, even though it need not be complete in its convex hull: a distinct same-parity pair in \(U_i\) has midpoint in \(\mathcal C_i\subseteq U_i\). Its full reflected row at \(c_{i,a}\) is exactly \(R_{i,a}\), because
\(R_{i,a}\subseteq U_i\cap(2c_{i,a}-U_i)\subseteq A_i\cap(2c_{i,a}-A_i)=R_{i,a}\).
Every other supported center has just its singleton reflected row. Each two-atom parity cell is labeled by its midpoint. There are precisely \(m_{i,a}\) label-\(a\) cells. Every nonhub atom is a cell endpoint; a hub is an endpoint precisely when it is a cross-member. Thus there are \(q_{\mathrm{ov},i}\) hub endpoints, and
\(k_{i,U_i}=m_{i,0}+m_{i,1}+2-q_{\mathrm{ov},i}\).
For one overlap, exactly one hub is a singleton cell, with either orientation possible. For two overlaps the cells form a partition into \(m_{i,0}+m_{i,1}\) pairs.

For every piece retain its exact raw normalizer, original mass, and conditional law:
$$
Z_{i,D}=\sum_{x\in D}w_{i,x},\qquad
\beta_{i,D}=\frac{Z_{i,D}}{Z_i},\qquad
\pi_{i,D}(x)=\frac{p_{i,x}}{\beta_{i,D}}
=\frac{w_{i,x}}{Z_{i,D}}\quad(x\in D).
\tag{7}
$$
All these masses are positive. For an overlapping union define, specifically under \(\pi_{i,U_i}\),
$$
\begin{aligned}
a_{i,a}&=\pi_{i,U_i}(c_{i,a}),&
S_{i,a}&=\sum_{x\in R_{i,a}\setminus\lbrace c_{i,a}\rbrace}\pi_{i,U_i}(x),\\
\mu_{i,a}&=\frac{S_{i,a}/a_{i,a}+2}{2(m_{i,a}+1)},&
A_{0,i,U_i}&=k_{i,U_i}^{\,2}\sum_{x\in U_i}\pi_{i,U_i}(x)^3,\\
\Delta_{i,a}&=4m_{i,a}(m_{i,a}+1)k_{i,U_i}^{\,2}a_{i,a}^3,&
A_{\mathrm{full},i,U_i}&=A_{0,i,U_i}+\Delta_{i,0}+\Delta_{i,1}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
$$
The means are unchanged if the ratios use \(p_i\), whereas the activity and full energy have the exact original-law expressions
$$
\begin{aligned}
A_{0,i,U_i}&=k_{i,U_i}^{\,2}\beta_{i,U_i}^{-3}\sum_{x\in U_i}p_{i,x}^3,\\
A_{\mathrm{full},i,U_i}&=k_{i,U_i}^{\,2}\beta_{i,U_i}^{-3}
\left[\sum_{x\in U_i}p_{i,x}^3+
\sum_{a=0}^1 4m_{i,a}(m_{i,a}+1)p_{i,c_{i,a}}^3\right].
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
$$
In particular the tests below never substitute the original factor count \(K_i\) or omit a conditional normalizer.

We next verify exhaustively the scalar coverage required for label selection. Suppress the factor index on an overlapping conditional union, writing \(X=U_i\), \(\pi=\pi_{i,U_i}\), \(k=k_{i,U_i}\), and \(m_a,a_a,S_a,\mu_a,A_0,\Delta_a,A_{\mathrm{full}}\) for (8). Let \(h_a=2m_a+1\). The globally affine law gives the exact identity \(\pi_u\pi_v=a_a^2\) in each label-\(a\) pair. Its probabilities have the form \(a_ae^{u_{a,r}},a_ae^{-u_{a,r}}\), where \(u_{a,r}=\ell_i\cdot(x-c_{i,a})\) for either chosen endpoint. Consequently
\(\mu_a=(1+\sum_{r=1}^{m_a}\cosh u_{a,r})/(m_a+1)\ge1\).
For \(\mathcal S\subseteq\lbrace0,1\rbrace\), set \(A_{\mathcal S}=A_0+\sum_{a\in\mathcal S}\Delta_a\).

On an active table, meaning \(A_0<1\), put \(d=-\log A_0\) and define
$$
r_a=\frac12\left[
\log\frac{A_0+\Delta_a}{A_0}+
\log\frac{A_{\mathrm{full}}}{A_0+\Delta_{1-a}}
\right]>0.
\tag{10}
$$
The scalar \(X,w_x,Z_X,\pi_x,k\) in 9b5e06469756fd2e are exactly \(U_i,w_{i,x},Z_{i,U_i},\pi_{i,U_i}(x),k_{i,U_i}\), and its scalar means, energies, and increments are precisely (8)-(10). For every one-overlap table, its proved scalar inequality (8) is already unconditional in means, pair counts, and full energy. It therefore gives
$$
d\le\sum_{a=0}^1\frac{B}{B+2\mu_a}r_a.
\tag{11}
$$
For a two-overlap table with \(\max(m_0,m_1)\ge D_\ast\), first suppose \(A_{\mathrm{full}}>9/8\). This is within the proved scalar coverage of 9b5e06469756fd2e, regardless of whether the means are comparable or disparate, so (11) follows. If \(A_{\mathrm{full}}\le9/8\) and \(\min(m_0,m_1)\ge100\), apply abb26eb9816cdb80. If \(A_{\mathrm{full}}\le9/8\) and \(\min(m_0,m_1)\le99\), choose its small-count label \(s\) and large-count label \(b\). Positivity gives \(1\le m_s\le99\), and \(m_b\ge D_\ast=2^{40}\), so 4b01e775176a9049 applies. Each of these last two accepted facts gives (11) with 256 in place of \(B\). Since \(b/(b+2\mu_a)\) increases with \(b>0\) and \(r_a>0\), it gives (11) with \(B=2^{80}\).

Here the alias maps to both abb26eb9816cdb80 and 4b01e775176a9049 are exact: their \(X,w_x,Z,p_x,K,A,A_{\mathrm{full}},m_a,a_a,S_a,\mu_a,\Delta_a,r_a\) are respectively \(U_i,w_{i,x},Z_{i,U_i},\pi_{i,U_i}(x),k_{i,U_i},A_{0,i,U_i},A_{\mathrm{full},i,U_i},m_{i,a},a_{i,a},S_{i,a},\mu_{i,a},\Delta_{i,a},r_a\). Counts mean all pairs, including each forced pair. The two forced pairs contain the other hub and have totals \(a_{1-a}+a_a^2/a_{1-a}\), precisely as those facts require. All actual nonforced weights remain arbitrary. No weights are equalized and no new law is introduced.

This split is exhaustive among the active tables assigned labels: one overlap is unrestricted; with two overlaps and maximum count at least \(D_\ast\), full energy is either \(>9/8\) or \(\le9/8\), and in the latter branch the minimum count is either \(\ge100\) or in \([1,99]\). Full-energy equality \(9/8\), count equality \(100\), and maximum-count equality \(D_\ast\) are included in their stated branches. No mean restriction remains. Two-overlap tables with maximum count \(<D_\ast\) will receive full rows instead and require no assertion of (11). Tables with \(A_0\ge1\) in the label block require no scalar inequality.

We derive simultaneous label budgets from (11), as in (9)-(12) of 9b5e06469756fd2e, to make their hypotheses explicit. Put \(f_a=B/(B+2\mu_a)\), choose \(\delta_0=\min(d,f_0r_0)\), \(\delta_1=d-\delta_0\), and set \(\gamma_a=r_a-\delta_a\). Then \(0\le\delta_a\le f_ar_a\), \(\delta_0+\delta_1=d\), and
$$
\delta_a\le Be^{-t_a}\gamma_a,\qquad
\gamma_a\ge\frac2{B+2}r_a>0,\qquad
t_a=\log(2\mu_a).
\tag{12}
$$
Indeed \(f_a/(1-f_a)=B/(2\mu_a)=Be^{-t_a}\) and \(1-f_a\ge2/(B+2)\). Direct cancellation in (10) gives \(r_0+r_1=\log A_{\mathrm{full}}+d\), so \(\gamma_0+\gamma_1=\log A_{\mathrm{full}}>0\). The positivity follows also from (11) and \(f_a<1\). Diminishing logarithmic increments give \(r_a\le\log((A_0+\Delta_a)/A_0)\). The empty, singleton, and full choices therefore give simultaneously
$$
\log A_{\mathcal S}\ge
\sum_{a\in\mathcal S}\gamma_a-
\sum_{a\notin\mathcal S}\delta_a
\qquad(\mathcal S\subseteq\lbrace0,1\rbrace).
\tag{13}
$$
For the singleton choice, the right side is \(r_a-d\); for the empty and full choices equality holds.

Select the full reflected row at a hub exactly when its label belongs to \(\mathcal S\), and use singleton rows at every other supported center. Use the oriented row convention of 445a9e668ee1a705. Exact pair equality makes the auxiliary geometric law at a full hub uniform on its \(h_a\) atoms, with score variance
\(V_{c_a}=(2/h_a)\sum_{r=1}^{m_a}u_{a,r}^2\).
The increasing concavity of \(v\mapsto\operatorname{arcosh}(v)^2\), proved in that fact, applied to the average of 1 and the \(\cosh u_{a,r}\), gives
\(V_{c_a}\le[2(m_a+1)/h_a]\operatorname{arcosh}(\mu_a)^2\le(4/3)t_a^2\).
It also covers \(\mu_a=1\) and zero variance. The selected scaled energy is exactly \(A_{\mathcal S}\). Its selected auxiliary variance price is
$$
\widehat\nu_{\mathcal S}
=\frac{k^2}{A_{\mathcal S}}\sum_{a\in\mathcal S}h_a^2a_a^3V_{c_a}
\le\frac3{2A_{\mathcal S}}\sum_{a\in\mathcal S}\Delta_at_a^2.
\tag{14}
$$
Here \(h_a^2/(h_a^2-1)\le9/8\), because \(h_a\ge3\). For a selected label set \(x=\Delta_a/A_0>0\). Then
\(\Delta_a/A_{\mathcal S}\le x/(1+x)\le\log(1+x)\le2r_a\).
The middle inequality follows by integrating \(1/(1+s)\ge1/(1+x)\) over \([0,x]\); the last uses positivity of the other logarithmic marginal in (10). Equations (12) and (14) therefore give the simultaneous budgets
$$
\delta_a\le C_{\mathrm{label}}e^{-t_a}\gamma_a,\qquad
\widehat\nu_{\mathcal S}
\le3\sum_{a\in\mathcal S}t_a^2r_a
\le\frac32(B+2)\sum_{a\in\mathcal S}t_a^2\gamma_a
\le C_{\mathrm{label}}\sum_{a\in\mathcal S}t_a^2\gamma_a.
\tag{15}
$$
Only (11) was used to derive (12)-(15); thus no comparable-mean allocation theorem has been applied outside its domain.

Fix a leaf \(\lambda=(D_1,\ldots,D_L)\in\prod_i\mathcal D_i\). Retain its support, original mass, conditional product law, and occupied capacity:
$$
\begin{aligned}
A_\lambda&=\prod_iD_i,&
\alpha_\lambda&=\prod_i\beta_{i,D_i},&
k_\lambda&=\prod_i k_{i,D_i},\\
P_\lambda(X)&=\prod_i\pi_{i,D_i}(x_i)
=\frac{\prod_iw_{i,x_i}}{\prod_iZ_{i,D_i}}
=\frac{P_X}{\alpha_\lambda}\quad(X\in A_\lambda).
\end{aligned}
\tag{16}
$$
Within this leaf only, abbreviate \(\pi_i=\pi_{i,D_i}\), \(k_i=k_{i,D_i}\), and \(A_{0,i}^{\lambda}=k_i^2\sum_{x\in D_i}\pi_i(x)^3\). The original \(p_i,P,Z_i,K_i\) remain those in (2).

Assign to the bounded block precisely those leaf factors that are two-overlap unions with \(\max(m_{i,0},m_{i,1})<D_\ast\), whether active or inactive. Give them all their full reflected rows. The hypotheses of c00bd51b9e53801c hold for each such conditional support and law: each parity class has at most two atoms and hence at most three; integral midpoints lie in the union; there are exactly \(m_{i,a}<D_\ast\) pairs with midpoint \(c_{i,a}\), and no pairs with any other midpoint; and affinity gives every exact pair identity. Its integer parameter \(D\) may therefore be fixed to the common \(D_\ast\). Its \(A,p,Z,K\) are respectively \(U_i,\pi_i,Z_{i,U_i},k_i\); its full-row \(H_p,b,\kappa,Y,V,q,\nu\) are exactly the full-row versions of the definitions below. Its \(C_D\) is \(C_{\mathrm{bound}}\) in (4), not a count of factors. Consequently, for every bounded factor,
$$
g_i:=\log\bigl(k_i^2b(\pi_i)\bigr)\ge0,
\qquad \nu_i\le C_{\mathrm{bound}}g_i.
\tag{17}
$$
This applies to its same conditional law with its same occupied count, regardless of activity or mean. It invokes the scalar full-row conclusion of c00bd51b9e53801c, rather than multiplying that fact's moment coefficients.

Every other leaf factor belongs to the label block. An inactive such factor uses singleton rows everywhere. Its scaled energy is \(A_{0,i}^{\lambda}\ge1\) and its price is zero. This includes all singleton factors and the boundary \(A_{0,i}^{\lambda}=1\).

An active one-center core receives one label. Translate its center \(c_i\) to zero. Its translated conditional law is \(e^{\ell_i\cdot u}/\overline Z_i\), where \(\overline Z_i=e^{-\ell_i\cdot c_i}Z_{i,D_i}\); translation preserves probabilities, scores, reflected quantities, and all ambient containing halfspaces. Take zero and one representative from each nonzero antipodal pair to form \(\mathcal B_i\), so \(|\mathcal B_i|=k_i\). The pair-count scalar result (16) in 60336390757d4ce6 applies. Its \(A,p,Z,M,B,\widetilde A_0,\widetilde d,\widetilde g,\nu\) are the translated core, translated \(\pi_i\), \(\overline Z_i\), \(k_i\), \(\mathcal B_i\), \(A_{0,i}^{\lambda}\), and the \(d_i,g_i,\nu_i\) in the next display. It gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mu_i&=\frac1{k_i}\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_i}\cosh(\ell_i\cdot b),&
t_i&=\log(2\mu_i),\\
d_i&=-\log A_{0,i}^{\lambda},&
g_i&=\log\bigl(k_i^2b(\pi_i)\bigr)>0,\\
d_i&\le2^{40}e^{-t_i}g_i,&
\nu_i&\le2^{40}t_i^2g_i.
\end{aligned}
\tag{18}
$$
Use the label parameters \(\delta_i=d_i\), \(\gamma_i=g_i\). Empty selection means all singleton rows and has logarithmic scaled energy \(-\delta_i\) and zero price; full selection means full rows and has energy \(\gamma_i\) and price \(\nu_i\). Since \(C_{\mathrm{label}}\ge2^{40}\), these are the one-label versions of (13) and (15).

An active overlapping union in the label block has either one overlap or two overlaps with maximum count at least \(D_\ast\). Its conditional law is exactly the scalar table already treated in (8)-(15). Give it two labels with their \(t_{i,a},\delta_{i,a},\gamma_{i,a}\). Selecting any subset selects precisely its corresponding full hub rows. Equations (13) and (15) hold for all four choices under this one law and its normalizer \(Z_{i,U_i}\).

Now use one binning over all labels of all active factors in the label block. For integers \(m\ge0\), let \(I_m\) comprise labels with parameter \(t\in[m,m+1)\), and let \(G_m=\sum_{e\in I_m}\gamma_e\), where \(e\) ranges over either kind of label. Each \(t\ge\log2\), and only finitely many labels occur. Retain all labels of a bin exactly when \(G_m\ge4C_{\mathrm{label}}(m+1)^2\). The simultaneous budgets allow this common selection even when two labels of one factor lie in different bins.

For a retained bin put \(W_m=C_{\mathrm{label}}(m+1)^2G_m\). Its price contribution is at most \(W_m\), and the retention threshold gives \(G_m\ge2\sqrt{W_m}\). A discarded bin loses at most
\(\sum_{e\in I_m}\delta_e\le C_{\mathrm{label}}e^{-m}G_m<4C_{\mathrm{label}}^2e^{-m}(m+1)^2\), unless it is empty, when the loss is zero. Since \(e^{-1}<1/2\) and \(\sum_{m\ge0}(m+1)^2r^m=(1+r)/(1-r)^3\), the total discarded loss is at most \(48C_{\mathrm{label}}^2\). Summing (13), its one-label counterpart, and the nonnegative inactive energies gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
S_{\mathrm{label}}&:=\sum_{i\text{ in label block}}\log(k_i^2\widehat b_i)
\ge\sum_{m\text{ retained}}G_m-48C_{\mathrm{label}}^2,\\
\nu_{\mathrm{label}}&:=\sum_{i\text{ in label block}}\widehat\nu_i
\le\sum_{m\text{ retained}}W_m,\\
S_{\mathrm{label}}&\ge2\sum_{m\text{ retained}}\sqrt{W_m}-48C_{\mathrm{label}}^2
\ge2\sqrt{\nu_{\mathrm{label}}}-48C_{\mathrm{label}}^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{19}
$$
Here \(\widehat b_i,\widehat\nu_i\) denote the selected energy and price, explicitly defined below. The square-root sum dominates the square root of its sum. Empty blocks, no active labels, and no retained bins satisfy the same inequalities with empty sums zero.

In the bounded block every row is full, so \(\widehat b_i=b(\pi_i)\) and \(\widehat\nu_i=\nu_i\). Equation (17) gives
\(S_{\mathrm{bound}}:=\sum_{i\text{ in bounded block}}g_i\ge0\) and
\(\nu_{\mathrm{bound}}:=\sum_{i\text{ in bounded block}}\nu_i\le C_{\mathrm{bound}}S_{\mathrm{bound}}\).
Consequently
$$
\begin{aligned}
S_{\mathrm{bound}}-2\sqrt{\nu_{\mathrm{bound}}}
&\ge S_{\mathrm{bound}}-2\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{bound}}S_{\mathrm{bound}}}\\
&=\bigl(\sqrt{S_{\mathrm{bound}}}-\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{bound}}}\bigr)^2-C_{\mathrm{bound}}
\ge-C_{\mathrm{bound}}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{20}
$$
This also covers zero full logarithmic energy, which forces zero price. Let
\(S_{\mathrm{total}}=\sum_i\log(k_i^2\widehat b_i)=S_{\mathrm{label}}+S_{\mathrm{bound}}\) and
\(\nu_{\mathrm{total}}=\sum_i\widehat\nu_i=\nu_{\mathrm{label}}+\nu_{\mathrm{bound}}\).
Using \(\sqrt{x+y}\le\sqrt x+\sqrt y\), (19)-(20) combine before any moment conversion to give
$$
S_{\mathrm{total}}-2\sqrt{\nu_{\mathrm{total}}}
\ge-48C_{\mathrm{label}}^2-C_{\mathrm{bound}}.
\tag{21}
$$
Thus the two types of factors have incurred one total absolute loss, independently of their number.

For completeness, verify the selected reflected source under precisely the conditional product law (16). This is the selected-row version of the source mechanism in 445a9e668ee1a705, also proved in 9b5e06469756fd2e. At every supported center \(j\in D_i\), let \(\widehat R_{i,j}\) be the row just selected, either the full reflected row in \(D_i\) or its singleton \(\lbrace j\rbrace\). Define
$$
\begin{aligned}
\widehat H_i(j)&=\sum_{x\in\widehat R_{i,j}}
\sqrt{\pi_i(x)\pi_i(2j-x)},&
\widehat b_i&=\sum_j\pi_i(j)\widehat H_i(j)^2,\\
\widehat\kappa_{i,j}(x)&=\frac{\sqrt{\pi_i(x)\pi_i(2j-x)}}{\widehat H_i(j)},&
\widehat q_{i,j}&=\frac{\pi_i(j)\widehat H_i(j)^2}{\widehat b_i},\\
Y_{i,j}(x)&=\tfrac12\log\frac{\pi_i(x)}{\pi_i(2j-x)},&
\widehat V_{i,j}&=\mathbb E_{\widehat\kappa_{i,j}}Y_{i,j}^2,
\qquad \widehat\nu_i=\sum_j\widehat q_{i,j}\widehat V_{i,j}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{22}
$$
Both nonzero orientations occur in row sums and the central atom occurs once. Every row includes \(j\), so its normalizer and \(\widehat b_i\) are positive. These auxiliary laws leave \(\pi_i(x)=w_{i,x}/Z_{i,D_i}\) unchanged. Reflection preserves \(\widehat\kappa_{i,j}\) and negates \(Y_{i,j}\), yielding score mean zero. A singleton row has \(\widehat H_i(j)=\pi_i(j)\) and zero price. At a full affine row \(\widehat H_i(j)=|\widehat R_{i,j}|\pi_i(j)\), and its auxiliary law is uniform. These identities show that (22) is exactly the energy and price used in (14)-(20), without any orientation or normalization change. In particular, with \(h_{i,a}=2m_{i,a}+1\), selecting a full hub changes its atomic contribution \(k_i^2a_{i,a}^3\) to \(k_i^2h_{i,a}^2a_{i,a}^3\), which is precisely the increment \(\Delta_{i,a}\) in (8).

For \(J=(j_i)\in A_\lambda\), put
\(\widehat R_J=\prod_i\widehat R_{i,j_i}\),
\(\widehat H_\lambda(J)=\prod_i\widehat H_i(j_i)\),
\(\widehat\kappa_J=\bigotimes_i\widehat\kappa_{i,j_i}\),
\(Y_J(X)=\sum_iY_{i,j_i}(x_i)\), and
\(\sigma_J^2=\sum_i\widehat V_{i,j_i}\).
Independence, the zero score means, and direct substitution imply
$$
\mathbb E_{\widehat\kappa_J}Y_J=0,\qquad
\mathbb E_{\widehat\kappa_J}Y_J^2=\sigma_J^2,\qquad
P_\lambda(X)=\widehat H_\lambda(J)\widehat\kappa_J(X)e^{Y_J(X)}
\quad(X\in\widehat R_J).
\tag{23}
$$
The law on the left is exactly \(\prod_iw_{i,x_i}/\prod_iZ_{i,D_i}\). An ambient closed halfspace containing \(J\) contains at least one endpoint of each noncentral orbit \(\lbrace X,2J-X\rbrace\), as well as \(J\) itself. Summing the smaller endpoint mass over these disjoint orbits gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
\tau_{P_\lambda}(J)
&\ge\frac12\sum_{X\in\widehat R_J}
\min\left\lbrace P_\lambda(X),P_\lambda(2J-X)\right\rbrace\\
&=\frac{\widehat H_\lambda(J)}2\mathbb E_{\widehat\kappa_J}e^{-|Y_J|}
\ge\frac{\widehat H_\lambda(J)}2e^{-\sigma_J}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{24}
$$
The factor one half cancels the two orientations of each noncentral orbit and uses only half the available central mass. Jensen followed by Cauchy--Schwarz proves the last step. This is valid for every ambient containing halfspace, including lower affine rank and \(\sigma_J=0\).

For \(\widehat q=\bigotimes_i\widehat q_i\), direct factorization yields
\(P_\lambda(J)\widehat H_\lambda(J)^2=(\prod_i\widehat b_i)\widehat q_J\) and
\(\mathbb E_{\widehat q}\sigma_J^2=\nu_{\mathrm{total}}\).
Square (24), average against the entire conditional product law, and apply Jensen and Cauchy--Schwarz once more. Using (21), this gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
M_2(P_\lambda)
&\ge\frac14\left(\prod_i\widehat b_i\right)\mathbb E_{\widehat q}e^{-2\sigma_J}\\
&\ge\frac14\left(\prod_i\widehat b_i\right)e^{-2\sqrt{\nu_{\mathrm{total}}}}\\
&=\frac1{4k_\lambda^2}\exp\left(S_{\mathrm{total}}-2\sqrt{\nu_{\mathrm{total}}}\right)

The coefficient is uniform over all mixed leaves. No factorwise moment coefficients have been multiplied.

Finally return to the original law \(P\). The leaves partition its support, \(\sum_\lambda\alpha_\lambda=1\), and the exact capacity sums give

For \(J\in A_\lambda\), every ambient closed halfspace containing \(J\) satisfies

$$

\ge c\sum_\lambda\frac{\alpha_\lambda^3}{k_\lambda^2},\\
1=\sum_\lambda\alpha_\lambda
&=\sum_\lambda\frac{\alpha_\lambda}{k_\lambda^{2/3}}k_\lambda^{2/3}
\le\left(\sum_\lambda\frac{\alpha_\lambda^3}{k_\lambda^2}\right)^{1/3}
\left(\sum_\lambda k_\lambda\right)^{2/3}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{26}
$$
Holder's inequality with exponents 3 and 3/2 gives the last line. It implies \(M_2(P)\ge c\mathcal K^{-2}\), retaining every outside mass in its original \(P_X=\prod_iw_{i,x_i}/\prod_iZ_i\). \(M_3(P)=\mathbb E_P(\tau_P^2)^{3/2}\ge M_2(P)^{3/2}\), proving (5).

The convex hull of a finite Cartesian product equals the product of its factor convex hulls: the nontrivial inclusion follows by multiplying the finite convex-combination coefficients in the factors. Intersecting with \(\mathbb Z^N\), and using the established factor completeness, proves the product completeness assertion. Singleton factors, entirely atomic leaves, empty blocks, zero score variances, and lower affine rank were all included in the source and capacity arguments. The exhaustive scalar split and the bounded-block treatment impose no residual restriction on any two-overlap conditional union.
